title: The Paper Shoal
logline: A cartography official keeps a crucial trade lane officially marked as an impassable asteroid shoal to protect the refueling profits of waystation merchants.

roles.description: Supervises the sector hydrographic bureau; polished, defensive, deeply invested in preserving stable shipping lanes.
An unaccredited acoustic probe operator who noticed the supposed asteroid belt contains mostly empty vacuum.
The consortium of merchant platforms situated along the forty-hour detour route around the supposed hazard.
The independent logistics pilots who burn a third of their profit margins taking the mandatory long detour.
An automated navigational beacon depot stationed at the edge of the charted asteroid hazard zone.
A sprawling orbital bazaar and fuel depot that caters exclusively to detour freight traffic.
The union shipping terminal where freight pilots take on bulk contracts.

public_situation: Every vessel crossing {system} takes a forty-hour detour around the Iron Shoal, paying premium propellant prices at {role:syndicate_waystation}.
private_truth: {role:cartography_warden} takes quarterly stipends from {role:waystation_syndicate} to keep the Iron Shoal officially classified as an active navigational hazard long after the debris dispersed.

beats.public_change: {role:independent_surveyor} posts a call for replacement telemetry sensors at {role:freight_exchange} after her probes are seized.

missions.reason: She needs high-grade sensor calibration parts purchased off-station and brought to the perimeter depot to finish mapping the empty corridor.
missions.private_fact: She is running out of food rations in the observation module and cannot afford dock fees anywhere else.

beats.public_change: The surveyor begins active radar pings into the hazard zone; {role:cartography_warden} issues a public warning that scanning uncertified lanes is illegal.

missions.reason: She needs an outside ship to fly three scan vectors through the heart of the charted shoal and document the complete lack of collision hazards.
missions.private_fact: She was expelled from the hydrographic academy years ago and wants revenge on the warden just as much as truth for the miners.

beats.public_change: {role:waystation_syndicate} offers an open bounty for 'stolen hydrographic records' and invites the pilot to meet at {role:syndicate_waystation}.

missions.reason: The warden asks the pilot to collect a confidential registry dossier from his private suite and return it without opening the seal.
missions.private_fact: The dossier contains bank receipts proving every director of {role:waystation_syndicate} has funded his private villa.

beats.public_change: The freight guild discovers proof of the empty lane and gathers in force outside the hydrographic offices.

missions.reason: She needs the verified scan plates delivered to the guild delegates before the syndicate can bribe station magistrates to confiscate them.
missions.private_fact: She intends to sell exclusive rights to the shortcut route if the guild does not offer her a lifetime pension.

player_choice.prompt: The pilot holds the proof that the shoal is empty and the receipts linking the warden to the merchants. How should the map be redrawn?

options.label: Release the true survey to the freight guild
Hand the evidence to the waystation syndicate for a cash settlement
Allow the warden to quietly update the charts as a newly cleared path

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot delivers the true survey to the freight guild.
resolutions.summary: The true charts are published. Freighters pour through the open corridor, fuel prices at {role:syndicate_waystation} collapse, and {role:cartography_warden} is removed.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot proved the deadly Iron Shoal was empty vacuum and broke the waystation fuel cartel.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot accepts the syndicate's settlement and buries the survey.
resolutions.summary: {role:waystation_syndicate} incinerates the radar data. The detour remains mandatory, fuel profits soar, and {role:independent_surveyor} is run out of the system.

consequences.public_summary: Dockworkers whisper that a pilot sold the safe route survey to the waystation kings for a private fortune.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot lets the warden reclassify the shoal as naturally dissipated.
resolutions.summary: {role:cartography_warden} logs the lane as newly cleared, opening the shortcut without facing fraud inquiries or paying back-rebates to the miners.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot abandons the contract or survey readings fail.
resolutions.summary: The Iron Shoal remains marked as impassable. Cargo haulers burn fuel on the detour, and {role:waystation_syndicate} maintains their artificial monopoly.

loose_threads.detail: The fuel board at {role:syndicate_waystation} lists a forty percent rebate for ships holding registry bonds issued by the warden's family firm.
The radar reflector at {role:shoal_marker_depot} broadcasts recorded rock echoes on an automated twelve-minute playback loop.
The dock manifest at the registry depot lists an inspector assigned to monitor the shoal who hasn't checked in since three governors ago.

radio_hooks: Fuel merchants at {role:syndicate_waystation} raise prices again, citing 'debris hazard transit surcharges'.
Independent haulers threaten to blockade {role:shoal_marker_depot} over falsified navigation advisories.
{role:cartography_warden} insists the Iron Shoal remains dangerous to all civilian hull configurations.

voice_direction.cartography_warden: Stately, condescending, and patronizingly patient. Speaks like an elder statesman explaining basic reality to unruly children, avoiding any direct discussion of kickbacks.
voice_direction.independent_surveyor: Nervous, biting, and relentlessly sarcastic. Her voice is frayed with exhaustion and caffeine, spitting out technical coordinates with vindictive precision.
